- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — if last 3–5 prices are rising sharply, cap forecast increase to 1–2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7), forecast should align with recent 10-day moving average — avoid long-term trend extrapolation.
- Correct for lag: if true outcome is > 10% above forecast, check if sentiment was bullish 2–3 days prior — if yes, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > 5% above 10-day average, flag for downward correction — especially if sentiment is fading or mixed.
